newsitem.title: USA: Bund futures see active first day trade at CBOT.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures see active first day trade at CBOT.

text.p: German Bund futures did brisk opening day business at the Chicago Board of Trade on Friday, but industry leaders said the big payoff in the CBOT-LIFFE link would come with the arrival of a unified European economy.
The CBOT launched open-outcry trading in Bund derivatives following the inaugural session for U.S. Treasury bond futures and options in London on Friday.
Trade began under a linkage agreement with the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange that was more than a decade in the making.

CBOT officials estimated first-day volume in Bunds at 16,000 futures and 500 options. Earlier, at a ceremony before the launch here, CBOT Chairman Patrick Arbor said 5,100 U.S. Treasury futures and 1,400 options had traded during the first LIFFE link session earlier in the day.

Floor traders said they were impressed with the initial participation in Bunds, which trade in a pit similar in size to the one used for federal funds futures, one of the smaller pits on the floor. Traders packed the Bund pit for the 1020 CDT (1520 GMT) opening to the extent that some who wanted to get in on the action were unable to secure a spot.
"I came down to trade it but couldn't get in the pit," said one CBOT member who normally trades from off the floor. He added he would try again next week.

Order flow was heaviest during the first two hours, which overlapped with LIFFE's APT electronic system and the Deutsche Terminboerse session, creating arbitrage opportunities between the three exchanges, traders said.
A handful of U.S. banks and brokerage firms were the day's biggest players, executing orders ranging from several hundred up to 1,000 contracts in size, pit sources said.
LIFFE Deputy Chairman Mark Eynon, in Chicago for the launch, said the stage was being set for a European government bond market that would rival the U.S. Treasury market in size.
"When monetary union takes place, we will look at a Euro bond contract, which opens immense opportunity for our business here and in Europe," Eynon told reporters.
The exchange leaders said they expect to add 10-year U.S. Treasury notes and long-term U.K. and Italian debt to the linkage in the next few months.
"What we're doing is listing the two more important ones first," Eynon said.
Arbor said the CBOT still hoped eventually to list Japanese government bond futures. The Tokyo Stock Exchange and LIFFE have a trading link of their own, he noted.
"We're working on developing a JGB contract here in Chicago," Arbor said.
A senior Deutsche Bank official, who said his bank planned to use the CBOT bund contract, also emphasized the importance of EMU to the success of the link.
"My guess is over time it will pick up a decent head of steam" as EMU nears, he said. European monetary union is planned for 1999.
